children: Apple has updated its Maps application to make Lake America searchable for U.S. users, while the label above the Canadian border remains Lake Ontario.
The move follows Google's decision to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America on its map application after President Trump renamed the lake in an executive order last week.
Google has said users in the U.S. will see "Lake America," while users in Canada will see "Lake Ontario." Users outside of both countries will see both names.

The two tech giants took similar steps after Trump renamed the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America at the beginning of his second term, and other U.S. executives also followed suit. Users of Google and Apple map applications in the U.S. see the Gulf of America name, while users in Mexico still see Gulf of Mexico.

The U.S. and Canada are locked in a bruising international trade dispute. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney walked away from trade negotiations after saying the U.S. sought a "bad deal." The Trump administration subsequently imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods, prompting a similar response from Carney.

Trump then changed the name of the lake and threatened additional levies, although the next phase of tariffs won't take effect until Jan. 1, meaning the two countries have additional time to negotiate.

On Saturday, Trump posted an AI video of animated ducks with hair that resembles his holding machine guns and defending "Lake America." He also posted another AI video showing him replacing a sign that said "Welcome to Lake Ontario" with one that says "Welcome to Lake America," and then dancing to the tune of "Y.M.C.A."

Canadian leaders have responded by saying the lake has been "Lake Ontario" for hundreds of years and will continue to be "Lake Ontario." Ontario Premier Doug Ford said on Sunday Trump's decision to rename the lake is "something out of 'Saturday Night Live.'"
Google and Apple have said they update maps with the U.S.'s Geographic Names Information System, which updates its labels when the federal government changes place names.
